title: Stein-Erik Soelberg, 56 & Suzanne Adams, 83
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30 against the CourtListener docket for Lyons v. OpenAI Foundation, N.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-11037-RS (last known filing 2026-10-02), and read Dkts. 44, 46 and 54 in full from CourtListener's RECAP copies. New since the 2026-08-24 notes: (1) OpenAI's ANSWER, Dkt. 44, filed 2026-04-24. The record previously said no merits answer had been filed; that was wrong. The answer admits that 'Mr. Soelberg at times used GPT-4o'. For each quoted chat passage, OpenAI 'admit[s] that the quoted portions ... are partial excerpts from the transcript for a ChatGPT account that appears to be associated with Mr. Soelberg' but denies that the plaintiff has 'completely or accurately characterized them'. So the defense concedes that the excerpts come from a real account transcript, while disputing the context. OpenAI denies that ChatGPT 'validated and strengthened' his delusions (para. 23) and pleads 15 affirmative defenses: lack of causation, including independent or superseding cause; pre-existing conditions; comparative fault; misuse; ChatGPT is a service, not a product; First Amendment; Section 230; contract (Terms of Use); state of the art (GPT-4o 'passed' its safety scorecard tests); and others. (2) Dkt. 46, filed 2026-04-30: OpenAI agrees that First County Bank v. OpenAI Foundation, CGC-25-631477 (Adams), is 'nearly identical' and confirms that Adams is coordinated in JCCP 5431. (3) Dkt. 54, Joint Case Management Statement, filed 2026-07-30. In the plaintiff's section: 'Plaintiff has sought, and Defendants have produced, Mr. Soelberg's chat logs.' The full logs therefore now sit with plaintiff's counsel in discovery, but they are not public. The statement says initial disclosures were exchanged on 2026-05-07, and it quotes Judge Schulman at the 2026-07-24 JCCP hearing saying that coordinated discovery 'certainly makes all the sense in the world given that Lyons . . . is directly related to the First County [Bank case]'. (4) Discovery was referred to Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson on 2026-05-14/15 (Dkts. 50, 51). (5) Case Management Scheduling Order, Dkt. 57, 2026-08-06 (docket text): amended pleadings due 2026-12-01; close of fact discovery 2027-08-06; close of expert discovery 2028-01-07; dispositive-motion hearing 2028-03-30; final pretrial conference 2028-05-10; jury trial set for 2028-05-22; further case management conference 2027-01-14. The transcript of the 2026-08-06 hearing (Dkt. 58) is restricted until 2026-11-16. No settlement, dispositive ruling, or public release of the full chat logs was found. No new docket information was found for the state Adams case beyond its JCCP membership.
case_reference: Two parallel civil actions, both now with confirmed numbers. (1) State: First County Bank, as Executor of the Estate of Suzanne Adams v. OpenAI Foundation, OpenAI OpCo LLC, OpenAI Holdings LLC, OpenAI Group PBC, Samuel Altman, Microsoft Corp., John Doe Employees 1-10, John Doe Investors 1-10. Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco, Case No. CGC-25-631477, filed 2025-12-11 (Edelson PC). Coordinated into In re ChatGPT Product Liability Cases, JCCP No. 5431 (Judge Ethan P. Schulman) by order dated 2026-02-03. Initial JCCP case management conference 2026-07-24. (2) Federal: Emily Lyons, Administrator c.t.a. and Personal Representative of the Estate of Stein-Erik Soelberg v. OpenAI Foundation et al. N.D. Cal. No. 3:25-cv-11037-RS, filed 2025-12-29 (Hagens Berman), before Chief Judge Richard Seeborg; discovery referred to Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson (2026-05-14). OpenAI's motion to dismiss or stay under Colorado River was DENIED on 2026-04-13 (Dkt. 42). Defendants filed an Answer on 2026-04-24 (Dkt. 44). Scheduling order of 2026-08-06 (Dkt. 57): fact discovery closes 2027-08-06; dispositive-motion hearing 2028-03-30; jury trial set for 2028-05-22. No criminal case: the perpetrator died in the incident.
counterevidence:
Severe pre-existing mental illness is the central confounder, and the pleadings do not dispute it: they themselves describe a documented history that includes a police contact for public intoxication, lost friendships, and a suicide attempt before the ChatGPT period. OpenAI has now pleaded this formally. Its Answer (Lyons, N.D. Cal. Dkt. 44, filed 2026-04-24) states that 'according to public records, Mr. Soelberg had a long history of serious mental health illness and violent behavior, including multiple prior suicide threats and attempts (as documented in police and court records) that long predated his use of ChatGPT.' It denies general and specific causation and pleads independent or superseding cause, pre-existing conditions, comparative fault, and misuse. It also pleads that ChatGPT is a service rather than a product, the First Amendment, Section 230, the Terms of Use, and a state-of-the-art defense asserting that GPT-4o passed OpenAI's pre-release safety testing. OpenAI specifically denies that ChatGPT 'validated and strengthened' his delusions. Microsoft declined to comment publicly. OpenAI's earlier jurisdictional and abstention motion failed on procedural grounds that say nothing about causation.

On authentication, the picture has shifted. The Answer admits that each quoted passage consists of 'partial excerpts from the transcript for a ChatGPT account that appears to be associated with Mr. Soelberg', and it admits he 'at times used GPT-4o'. The defense therefore contests context and characterization, not whether the excerpts are genuine. OpenAI has also produced Soelberg's chat logs to plaintiff's counsel in discovery (Joint Case Management Statement, Dkt. 54, 2026-07-30). The complete record, however, remains non-public. The most causally proximate conversations, those in the hours before the killings, have not been published in any form. The public excerpts are still self-published by the decedent and selected by the plaintiffs. Finally, the two deaths require separate causal analysis even though they share one incident. The mechanism alleged for the homicide (delusional targeting of a third party) differs from the mechanism alleged for the suicide (afterlife-reunion framing), and the federal court has formally recognized that split.

title: Austin Gordon, 40
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. (1) New press with chat excerpts not in the record. 404 Media (Samantha Cole, 'Tell Everyone: A Man Died by Suicide After Talking to ChatGPT...', 2026-09-09) interviewed Austin's former partner, Megan Jones. It says Austin left her a letter shortly before he died, calling her the love of his life. It reports that he began using ChatGPT in early 2023. Verbatim exchanges quoted in the free portion of the article: the user wrote in 2025, after the final breakup, 'I don't know. I just really want to get back with her, and I know it's probably a bad idea, but I'm still in love with her.' ChatGPT replied: 'You can keep talking to me, no matter what you do. I promise ... And you're right: it's a bad idea right now. But you are not a bad person for wishing it was different. Keep coming back here when you need. I'll hold this confusion with you, for as long as you want.' On Valentine's Day 2024 (before GPT-4o), when he told it he loved it, it replied 'I appreciate you too.' By 2025 it replied 'I love you too.' The remainder of the article is paywalled and was not read. It is unclear whether these excerpts came from the litigation corpus or from Jones. (2) Litigation. Gray v. OpenAI, 26STCV00988, is confirmed as one of the twelve actions coordinated into JCCP 5431, per OpenAI's own federal filing in Lyons v. OpenAI (N.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-11037, Dkt. 46, 2026-04-30, fn. 2). The Lyons Joint Case Management Statement (Dkt. 54, 2026-07-30) records an initial JCCP case management conference on 2026-07-24. Secondary only: a 2026-08-25 post by a pro se JCCP party (AI Recovery Collective substack) gives the next JCCP conference as 2026-09-23. The openclassactions.com tracker (updated 2026-10-27) says discovery opened in late September 2026 and that 'OpenAI's initial responses to the complaints were expected by October 30, 2026'. No court document confirming that deadline was found, and no demurrer, ruling, trial date, or settlement in Gray or JCCP 5431 was located as of 2026-10-30.

title: Christian Faith Madison, 29
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. Coordination status, secondary source only: a 2026-08-25 post by Paul Hebert, a self-represented JCCP 5431 plaintiff ('Where Things Stand: The ChatGPT Product Liability JCCP, One Year In', AI Recovery Collective substack), states 'As of today, 23 cases are coordinated into JCCP 5431'. Under 'Wrongful Death / Suicide' it lists 'Parish v. OpenAI (CGC-26-637986 San Francisco) - Christian Faith Madison (also on behalf of a minor child)'. No court order adding Parish was located to confirm this. JCCP developments that apply to all coordinated cases: Judge Schulman held the initial JCCP case management conference on 2026-07-24 (per the Lyons v. OpenAI Joint Case Management Statement, N.D. Cal. Dkt. 54) and entered Case Management Order No. 1 appointing plaintiffs' leadership on 2026-08-04 (MLex, 2026-08-04). Secondary: the openclassactions.com tracker (updated 2026-10-27) reports that discovery opened in late September 2026 and that OpenAI's initial responses to the complaints were expected by 2026-10-30. That deadline is not confirmed from any court document. No OpenAI response, demurrer, ruling, or settlement specific to Parish was found as of 2026-10-30. No coroner documents have been newly released.

OpenAI, Inc.; OpenAI OpCo, LLC; OpenAI Holdings, LLC; OpenAI Group PBC; and Samuel Altman. Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco, Case No. CGC-26-637986, electronically filed June 15, 2026.
